document.abstract: This paper begins with a review of the wide range of digital audio origination, storage and processing devices coming into use in editing suites. It points out the need for a centralized workstation to manage the control and interconnection of these devices, and the need for unified and simplified control of audio similar to the universal control employed in video editing. A system is presented which makes use of recent advances in digital signal processing and interface standardization to provide a compact and comprehensive audio “paint” station.

authors.bio: Oliver Morgan was educated in England at Winchester College and Oxford University. He worked first in the telecommunications and computer industries, then moved to the television industry in 1981. After a number of years with the Convergence Corporation in Europe as engineering project manager, he transferred to the U.S. when the company was acquired by EECO Inc. He is now manager of new product development for EECO's video division, specializing in the planning and design of systems for post-production applications.
